title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, alerts, runbooks, retrospective & Q2 2026 roadmap
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose
- Provide a single reference for the Platform team that covers: dashboards to monitor core services, alerting thresholds and policies, operational runbooks for common incidents, a short retrospective of recent incidents, and the Q2 2026 roadmap for systems & services.

Scope
- Applies to "runtime-gateway", "control-plane-api", "kv-cache-service", "model-router", and platform-level infrastructure (cluster-autoscaler, ingress, and monitoring stack).
- Intended readers: platform engineers, on-call SREs, and engineering managers.

Ownership & Contacts
- Platform systems owner: Marcus Nguyen (email: marcus@redwood.ai)
- Observability owner: Elena García (email: elena@redwood.ai)
- On-call rotation: platform-oncall@redwood.ai (pager duty: Platform-Oncall)
- Secondary escalation: Samir Khan (lead, runtime)

Dashboards (what to look at)
- Production Overview (grafana: platform/prod-overview): single-pane summary for P99 latency, error rate, request rate, GPU utilization, and free capacity in dedicated pools.
- Control Plane Health (grafana: platform/control-plane-health): API errorrate, leader elections, DB replication lag, control-plane API 95/99 latencies.
- Runtime Gateway Metrics (grafana: platform/runtime-gateway): tail latency (P50/P95/P99), inflight request count, succeeded/failed token generation, KV-cache hit ratio.
- Cost & Capacity (grafana: platform/capacity-cost): reserved GPU utilization, spot preemption rate, per-model throughput, batching efficiency.

Dashboard detail (example panels & thresholds)
- Panel: runtime-gateway P99 latency — target: < 350ms. Alert if > 500ms for 5m.
- Panel: control-plane-api 5xx rate — target < 0.5% of requests. Alert if > 1% for 3m.
- Panel: kv-cache hit ratio — target > 85% on production traffic. Alert if < 75% for 10m.

Alerting policy (high level)
- Severity mapping:
  1) Sev-0 (P0): platform-wide outages (control-plane unavailable for >5m, >30% request failure across regions). Immediate page to Platform-Oncall and Execs.
  2) Sev-1 (P1): Significant degradation affecting SLAs or major customers (model-router capacity exhausted, P99 > 2s). Page Platform-Oncall.
  3) Sev-2 (P2): Localized issues or elevated error rates. Notify on-call via Slack #platform-oncall and create a ticket.
  4) Sev-3 (P3): Informational/maintenance alerts. No immediate action required.

Alert rules (examples)
- control_plane_api_5xx_rate_high: trigger when rate > 1% for 3m -> Sev-1. Owner: control-plane team. Runbook: control-plane-api-runbook.
- runtime_gateway_p99_latency_spike: trigger when P99 latency > 500ms for 5m -> Sev-1. Owner: runtime team. Runbook: runtime-gateway-latency-runbook.
- kv_cache_miss_rate_high: trigger when miss rate > 25% for 10m -> Sev-2. Owner: runtime; possible remediation: flush cache / warm prefixes.

Runbooks (links + short summaries)
- runtime-gateway-latency-runbook (link: /confluence/eng-platform/runtime-gateway-latency-runbook-2026.json)
  1) Triage: Confirm alert via Grafana, check span traces in Tempo for slow requests.
  2) Check recent deploys: kubectl get deployments -n runtime; if a canary is live, rollback to previous revision.
  3) Inspect batching: query Redis metrics and per-model batch sizes. If batching config changed in the last 30m, revert.
  4) If GPU saturation: escalate to Samir Khan and consider temporarily shifting traffic to lower-cost model variant.

- control-plane-api-runbook (link: /confluence/eng-platform/control-plane-api-runbook-2026.json)
  1) Validate DB connectivity and leader status (kubectl exec /scripts/check-db.sh).
  2) Rotate tokens/credentials if error pattern indicates auth failures.
  3) If API is returning rate-limited errors due to quota, check rate-limiter service and request quota increases from infra.

Runbook excerpt: runtime P99 latency triage (quick commands)\n```
# check deployment age and restarts
kubectl -n runtime get pods -o wide --sort-by=.status.startTime
# recent logs for gateway
kubectl -n runtime logs deployment/runtime-gateway --since=15m | tail -n 200
# query prometheus for P99 latency over 15m window
curl -sG "$PROM_URL/api/v1/query" --data-urlencode "query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"runtime-gateway\"}[15m])) by (le))"
```

On-call rotation & escalation matrix
- Primary on-call: 1-week shift, starts Monday 09:00 UTC. Schedule in PagerDuty: Platform-Oncall (team).
- Secondary: 2-hour overlap for handoff, and on-call backup is paged if primary does not acknowledge in 10 minutes.
- Escalation order: primary -> secondary -> team lead (Marcus Nguyen) -> SRE manager -> Exec on-call.

How-tos (common ops tasks)
- Adding a dashboard
  1) Create dashboard in Grafana using the platform dashboard template (dashboard-id: template-platform-basic).
  2) Add panels with PromQL queries, set thresholds and annotation rules.
  3) Submit PR to observability-configs repo with dashboard JSON. Reviewers: Elena García, observability.
- Tuning an alert
  1) Propose new threshold with supporting metric history (at least 4 weeks).
  2) Present to weekly Observability sync for approval.
  3) Implement change in alerts repo and deploy with CI.
- Performing a safe rollback
  1) Confirm the last successful revision: kubectl rollout history deployment/<svc> -n <ns>.
  2) Rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<svc> --to-revision=<rev> -n <ns>.
  3) Monitor dashboards for 30 minutes.

Retrospective: Q1 -> early Q2 2026 (summary of incidents & Lessons learned)
- Incident A: Region control-plane outage (2026-03-12)
  - Impact: control-plane API returned 503 for 22 minutes in us-west-2; customer-facing API fallback kicked in for most users.
  - Root cause: DB failover triggered expensive snapshotting combined with a misconfiguration in leader-election timeout.
  - Actions completed: adjusted snapshot schedule, increased leader-election timeout to 15s, improved runbook for DB failover.
  - Owner: database/infra team.
- Incident B: Runtime latency regression after model-quantization rollout (2026-04-28)
  - Impact: P99 latency rose from 310ms -> 980ms for 45 minutes for high-length sequences.
  - Root cause: quantized kernel selection path had a fallback that disabled KV cache warming.
  - Actions completed: hotfix to restore warming path, additional canary checks added to model rollout pipeline, and a new preflight test that simulates long-sequence workloads.
  - Owner: serving-runtime.

Retrospective action items (status)
- Add model rollout preflight: DONE (serving-runtime).
- Add automated KV-cache warmers in canaries: IN_PROGRESS (ETA 2026-07-02).
- Increase observability retention for slow traces from 7d -> 14d: DONE.

Q2 2026 Roadmap (systems & services priorities)
- May 2026
  - Finish standardized platform dashboard templates and add cost attribution panels. Owner: observability.
- June 2026
  - Launch automated model rollout preflight and rollback hooks in CI (serving-runtime).
  - Implement advanced alert suppression rules for scheduled maintenance windows (platform).
- July 2026
  - Deploy per-tenant capacity quotas in Dedicated to prevent noisy neighbors (infra + platform).
  - Pilot on-prem observability agent that ships aggregated metrics to private control-plane for Private deployments.

Milestones & success metrics
- Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for Sev-1 alerts from 6m -> 3m by end of Q2.
- Reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) for runtime latency incidents by 30% via improved runbooks and preflight tests.
- Increase KV-cache hit ratio on p90 workloads from 80% -> 88% across production clusters.

Operational notes & conventions
- Dashboard naming convention: platform/<area>/<name> (e.g. platform/runtime/p99-latency).
- Alert naming convention: team_service_metric_condition (e.g. runtime_gateway_p99_latency_high).
- Runbook ownership: every runbook must list an owner and a last-reviewed date. Reviews scheduled quarterly.

Appendix: Links & artifacts
- Observability repo (dashboards + alerts): git@github.com:redwood/observability-configs.git
- Runbooks index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks-index-2026.json
- PagerDuty schedule: Platform-Oncall (internal)

If you are reading this as an on-call responder: follow the runbook for the alert, annotate the incident in the runbook (time acknowledged, actions taken), and create a post-incident ticket if the outage meets the create-incident threshold (see runbooks-index).
